Professional and Agency owners can edit their own Hosted portal settings in the
main app or while signed in to their active portal. A team member or agency
client cannot change the owner's portal. Professional owners can still set
general Workspace branding separately. Agency and Custom Domain White Label
Agency plans use their own portal configuration instead.
Decisionate product-update preferences are not shown on hosted portals; this
does not disable invitations, alerts or weekly report emails.

Choose the subdomain, portal name, support email, logo, colors and welcome
message. Set one logo by entering its public HTTPS image URL in Logo URL or
choosing Upload logo. Uploads must be PNG, JPEG or WebP and can be up to 1 MB.
That same logo appears in the portal preview, sign-in screen and browser tab;
there is no separate browser-icon upload. Existing icon-only images are kept as
the logo when no logo was previously selected. Removing the logo clears that
image too. PNG or WebP can preserve a transparent background; JPEG cannot. The
previously distributed black-backed Decisionate JPEG is recognized and replaced
with its original transparent PNG, including in saved portal previews. Other
uploaded logos keep their original pixels and backgrounds.
Published colors apply to the signed-in hosted portal: primary for key actions
and navigation, accent for secondary highlights, and background for the area
behind workspace content. Decisionate adjusts the background and text colors as
needed for readability in light or dark mode. The logo and colors also appear in
the agency owner's own workspace on app.decisionate.ca without changing client
workspaces on the main app. Save draft does not change the live workspace. Use
Preview portal and Publish changes to apply the new branding. Other open tabs
may need a reload.
An optional background image can be up to 128 KB.
The subdomain field checks whether your chosen address is available. Names are
case-insensitive, and each address belongs to only one agency. Use 3-40 letters,
numbers or single hyphens; platform names such as app and support cannot be used.
Save draft reserves the address; checking availability alone does not reserve it.
If someone else reserves it first, choose another name. An address already reserved
by an agency stays unavailable to others, including while its portal is paused or
retired. After saving, the subdomain input is hidden. The saved portal address
remains visible with a copy control and, when active, an Open portal button.
Your saved address cannot then be renamed in this screen.
Preview desktop or mobile, then explicitly activate or publish. Draft changes are
not live until published. Reopen setup to continue. Publishing registers the portal's
sign-in domain with Clerk. If shared sign-in setup is unavailable, save the draft
and contact support. No manual hosting, sign-in or email verification switches are
needed; the portal still needs working HTTPS, authentication and delivery services.

If publishing fails, your draft and reserved address remain safe; the portal does
not open without verified sign-in setup. Follow the displayed reason. Temporary
service or rate-limit failures can be retried. Credential, account-permission or
sign-in-address verification problems require platform support, not another
subscription, a different subdomain or a new Clerk account. A subdomain-only
plan does not require custom-domain provisioning.
The publishing error may include a Reference naming the failed setup step.
Share that reference with platform support; it contains no API keys. A paid
Clerk plan alone does not confirm that the API server uses the correct instance
or has permission to create its domains. Do not disconnect a Clerk integration
or replace your production keys just to clear an unexplained error.

The public portal welcome page offers Continue to sign in, not open registration.
People without a login should open their workspace invitation. Its sign-in page

and a pending invitation or existing membership.

Credential entry, verification and password recovery use the existing secure
Decisionate account flow, then return to the branded portal. When opened from an
active agency portal, the credentials page uses that agency's published name and
logo, including its browser-tab icon. It still uses the shared secure sign-in
address; there is no separate login account or Clerk instance. Switching between
sign-in and sign-up retains the agency and invited workspace. Direct Decisionate
sign-ins retain Decisionate branding. This presentation does not change shared
verification emails or third-party identity-provider consent screens.
The portal's Continue button carries its return address in the first credentials
request, even if Clerk generates a plain primary sign-in URL. This lets the agency
name and published logo appear immediately instead of changing after page load.
After authentication, Clerk must share the signed-in session with the agency
portal before opening the workspace. The portal return link requests that sync;
it does not bypass sign-in or workspace permissions. A successful return opens the
authorized workspace or invitation destination, not the welcome screen again.
Clients need the
normal workspace invitation and permission; signup alone does not grant access,
create another workspace or enroll a client in a subscription.
Manage invitations in Settings. An invitation to attach an existing independent
workspace starts on the main application before that workspace joins the agency.

title: Business Analysis: returns, profitability, customers, sales and cash

content:
Open Business Analysis and choose Return on spend to compare revenue earned
for each dollar already spent.

1. Set From, To and Currency for the period you want to review.
2. Answer Where are your revenue and spending figures stored? For Both in the same dataset, select the dataset,
   Revenue column and Spending column. Under Show separate results for, choose
   a column such as Channel for one result per channel, or All records combined
   for one overall result. For Revenue and spending in different datasets, name each
   comparison and select its Revenue dataset and Revenue column, then its
   Spending dataset and Spending column. Add comparison
   adds another channel or business to compare.
3. Review Date column and Records contain for each source. Choose a dimension
   filter when you want only a particular channel, product or location.
4. Answer Where do your revenue figures come from? Choose Sales records with one
   channel per sale or Each ad platform's own sales figures. Check the confirmation
   list: dates and currency match, revenue has refunds, discounts and tax removed,
   and spending is counted once. For your sales records, each sale is counted
   once under one channel and every channel uses the same tracking method. With ad-platform
   figures, acknowledge that the same sale may appear in more than one report.
5. Choose Compare results. Review revenue per dollar, spending and any missing
   data warnings. Choose Create decision to record an action right there, or
   Save comparison to keep the evidence without making a decision.

For example, 300 dollars of revenue divided by 100 dollars of spending gives
3 dollars of revenue per dollar spent. This is revenue return, not profit.
Show separate results for uses the categories already in your records. It does
not determine which channel generated a sale. All records combined includes
only the selected dates and any dimension filter, not the dataset's entire history.
For a fair channel ranking, each sale must be counted once under one channel, with the same tracking method used for every channel. Do not
give every channel the store's entire revenue. Independently platform-reported
sales can still be shown separately, but without declaring an overall winner.

For "which channel gave me more bang for my dollar?", open Business Analysis,
then Return on spend. This compares money already spent
with recorded revenue, not a future budget. It is available for any eligible
source, not only Meta, Google or Shopify.

Choose the historical dates and currency. With Both in the same dataset, choose
the revenue and spending columns. Under Show separate results for, select a
channel or campaign column for individual results; All records combined gives
one overall result within the selected dates and filters.
With Revenue and spending in different datasets, name each comparison and select its own revenue and
spending amounts. A dimension filter can select the channel's sales from a
shared sales dataset. Do not assign the entire store's revenue to every channel.

Daily totals need every date, including explicit zeros for no activity. Monthly
totals need complete months. Individual transactions may be sparse, but you must
confirm the selected period's records are complete. These controls are not time
groupings for a correlation analysis.

Revenue per dollar is total selected revenue divided by total spending. It is
not an average of daily returns, a correlation coefficient, a profit margin or
proof of incremental sales caused by advertising. Refunds and discounts should
already be accounted for in revenue, with tax excluded. All amounts must use
the same currency. Decisionate does not convert currencies here.

Choose Sales records with one channel per sale when each sale belongs to only
one channel and every channel uses the same tracking method. With Each ad
platform's own sales figures, returns are displayed separately without an overall
winner because the same sale may appear in more than one platform's report.
This release does not infer attribution from total store revenue or estimate
historical channel contributions from a model. Missing revenue links must be
resolved in the source records before a fair return comparison is available.

content:
Use Budget Planner to see whether changing how you divide your advertising budget could improve sales or orders, without increasing the total budget.

1. Open Analysis > Budget Planner. Choose the result you want to improve, such as store revenue or orders.
2. Add each spending option separately. For example, choose Google Ads spend and Meta Ads spend, with Shopify revenue as the result. You can use other eligible datasets or separate channel values in a dimension column; this is not limited to those providers.
3. In Set up budget, enter the total budget, currency, start Monday and number of planning weeks. Confirm the spending does not overlap and consider other business influences. Choose Preview budget to go straight to Results.
4. Review the recent spending mix beside the suggested test at the same total budget. If the data supports a recommendation, the preview shows suggested amounts and an estimated additional result with a range. If it does not, the planner explains what is missing instead of inventing a split.
5. If the checks fail, choose Edit setup and read which records or assumptions need attention. Otherwise save the supported plan, then use Create Decision to record what you will change, the expected result and a review date. You apply any spending changes yourself.

You need at least 104 complete matching weeks of recent history, plus enough separate variation in each option's spending. The data and model checks must pass before a mix is recommended. A recommendation is a test to review, not a guarantee of more sales or proof that a channel caused them. The planner never changes an advertising platform's budget automatically.

To find which channel gave more revenue per dollar in the past, use Business Analysis > Return on spend instead. That needs consistently assigned channel revenue as well as spending. Budget Planner is for deciding what to test next; Ask Decisionate explains the workflow but does not calculate your actual spending split in chat.

# Accounts, workspaces and access

A workspace is the boundary for datasets, connections, report evidence,
decisions, alert settings and AI context. Always check the workspace name before
analyzing data, changing settings or sharing a link.

Your email address is for signing in, invitations and notifications. A `usr_...`
value is the internal account reference, not a second login. Client workspace
references may also contain `:client:`; those identify workspaces, not people.
Production sign-in requires a verified email. When a Clerk login token omits it,
the API checks the account with Clerk rather than trusting a browser-supplied
email. Complete email verification before continuing if prompted.
Every production user account needs an email address. If an older account is
shown without an email, contact support to have an authorized administrator
recover its mapping. The same account ID and workspace data are preserved;
do not create a replacement account to work around the missing address.

Confirm that the client workspace exists, the client has accepted the appropriate
invitation and the required agency access has been granted. An authorized agency
owner can switch into that client's context for permitted analysis and decision
work. That context does not provide the client Data navigation for adding
datasets or connection parameters. Client owners normally work in their own
isolated workspace rather than an agency-wide workspace switcher.

Client users have the client-workspace data and analysis access supported for
their role. Granting agency-owner access remains a client-owner operation;
another client user or a support prompt cannot grant it implicitly.

In an active client workspace, the client owner can open Settings > Agency
connection and turn on Allow agency access. The managing agency owner can then
open the client workspace. Turn it off to revoke access without unlinking,
changing ownership, or changing billing. This is separate from Share workspace,
which invites an individual collaborator.

content:
In Settings > Client Workspaces, enter the client workspace name and Workspace
owner email, then choose Create and invite owner. This single action creates
the workspace and its owner invitation together and sends the invitation email
automatically; no separate invitation action is needed. The
email names the agency and client workspace and links
to the sign-in page, not directly to the dashboard. The link keeps the invited
workspace as the destination after sign-in. The client signs in or creates an account with
the invited email address and verifies it. After sign-in, Decisionate accepts
the pending invitation and opens the client workspace, not a new personal
workspace. A client owner or client user signing in without the invitation link
also defaults to their client workspace unless they already selected another
accessible client workspace. On a hosted agency portal, an unrelated signed-in
session leads to Accept your invitation. Choose Continue to sign in if you
already have a login, or Create your login otherwise. If asked to continue,
that action signs out the previous session and opens the chosen form. On the
standard sign-in page, choose Use invited account if shown. Use the email that
received the invitation. Merely opening the invitation does not sign anyone
out or grant access to the current account.

Link an existing workspace is a separate, collapsed option for a client who
already owns a workspace. Invite to agency asks that owner to approve linking
their existing workspace; it is not a second step when creating a new one.
If the email is already tied to another workspace through ownership, membership
or a pending invitation, Decisionate blocks a new workspace or email invitation.
Use Link an existing workspace to reconnect a former client without deleting
their data. To replace a workspace instead, only its owner can delete it.

For an existing pending invitation, the agency owner can select the client under
Settings > Client Workspaces and choose Resend invitation, or Send invitation
when its email was not confirmed. Check the recipient's
inbox and spam folder before sending again. There is a one-minute wait between
send attempts. Revoking an invitation removes that pending access.

An email problem does not undo client workspace creation. If the screen says the
invitation email was not confirmed, keep the existing workspace and use Send
invitation; do not create the client again. Email sent means the email service
accepted the message, not that it reached the inbox. If sending or verified-email
lookup remains unavailable, contact support. A paused client must be resumed
before an invitation can be sent or accepted.

content:
Before the client owner accepts their invitation, the agency owner can pause,
resume or delete the unused client workspace in Settings > Client Workspaces.
Pausing preserves its data and schedules but blocks access and background work.
Deletion requires typing the workspace name and permanently removes its data.

After the client accepts, the workspace belongs to that client owner. The agency
can still pause and resume the client workspace while it manages that client.
Only the managing agency owner can resume an agency-paused workspace; the client
owner and other client users cannot override that pause. A paused client owner
can choose Unlink agency, or contact the agency to resume access. Other client
users cannot unlink the workspace. Pausing preserves data and billing settings
but blocks data access and background work. The agency can manage this status
without being granted access to the client's data.

The agency cannot delete an accepted client's workspace, remove its owner or
take over member management. It sees Remove from agency instead. That action removes the
workspace from the agency's list and ends the agency's access and shared billing
for that workspace. It does not delete datasets, reports, decisions, connections,
members or the workspace itself. Workspace IDs and data IDs stay unchanged.
An active import, report analysis or AI request must finish before removal.

Manage client workspaces shows the current owner email, or the invited owner
and pending status before acceptance. Link an existing workspace is a separate
form for an owner who already has a workspace.

An active client owner can choose Share workspace in Settings to invite one
collaborator by email. The collaborator must verify the invited email before
getting access. The owner can resend or revoke a pending invitation and remove
an accepted collaborator. A pending invitation uses the same slot as an accepted
collaborator. Revoke it or remove current access before inviting another email.
Sharing does not give the collaborator ownership or
give the agency access to client data.

An active client owner can select Delete workspace in Settings without unlinking
first. While linked and paused, Unlink agency is the only available workspace action: deletion, trials,
direct subscription changes and analysis remain blocked. Unlinking requires confirmation,
removes the workspace from the agency's list and revokes its access without deleting data.
After unlinking, the owner can choose Delete workspace and type its name to confirm
permanent deletion, or continue independently with a trial or direct subscription.
Other client users and the agency cannot permanently delete an accepted workspace.
Deletion removes its data, connections, reports, decisions, matching records,
memberships, invitations and agency listing. The owner is signed out afterwards.
An app account with no remaining workspace or platform role is removed; shared
accounts and other workspaces are preserved. This does not delete the account
at the sign-in provider. Minimal email suppression and consent history is retained
to honor unsubscribe requests while email-provider cleanup is processed. A direct
paid subscription must be canceled in Billing before deletion. Removing a client
frees its used agency slot; it does not automatically reduce purchased capacity,
refund the agency or cancel the agency's subscription.
Queued imports and analyses are canceled as part of deletion. Work already running
must finish first; this protects against a worker recreating deleted data.

# Upload and inspect datasets

The file workflow offers CSV, JSON, Excel and Parquet ingestion, subject to the
readers installed in the deployment. A dataset's real schema comes from its
file or connector output, not from a generic example shown in a conversation.

title: Upload and inspect datasets

content:
Use stable column names and a header row for CSV. Include a genuine date or
timestamp when you need trends, relationships or forecasts. Numeric measures
need consistent units. Categories such as campaign, product or region belong in
dimension fields rather than being forced into numeric measures.

After processing, inspect the dataset name, row count, preview, date fields,
detected numeric columns and selected metrics. A numeric-looking identifier is
not automatically a sensible metric. A file containing twelve monthly records
does not contain daily observations merely because a date selector offers days.

title: Upload and inspect datasets

content:
Check the file format, actual worksheet or payload, column headers and imported
date range. For connector datasets, also check sync and backfill status. A
provider may return no records for a valid query because the account, dates or
permissions differ from the intended source.

Do not invent missing values, automatically interpret absent rows as zero
activity, or rename an unknown column to a familiar vendor field. If a source
schema changed, review the saved metric and date selections before recalculating.

content:
Dataset-level metric selection controls eligible analytical measures; a report
then chooses a subset of those measures. Non-metric date, category and identifier
fields can remain available for inspection or filtering without being plotted as
metrics. Removing a measure from a chart is not a guarantee that its raw source
column has been deleted from storage.

content:
Uploading data file means the file is still being sent. Preparing your dataset
means the file was received and is being processed in the background. The file
name stays visible so you can identify which import is being checked.

The transfer has a five-minute window, separate from normal page requests.
Temporary failures when checking an accepted import are retried without sending
the file again. A timeout or lost confirmation does not prove the import failed:
check the dataset list before uploading the same file again. A confirmed import
failure still shows its error rather than being treated as success.

Empty files, unsupported formats and files larger than 100 MB are rejected
before the browser sends them. If the import worker is unavailable or five
imports are already queued for the workspace, try again once it is available
or the existing imports finish. After a confirmed import, the dataset list is
refreshed so a recently cached list does not hide the new dataset.

For large CSVs, a Parquet copy can be substantially smaller while preserving the
same rows and columns. Upload the actual data file, not a ZIP bundle. A daily
summary is not the same as the original order-level or line-level dataset;
choose the level of detail needed for your analysis.

4. Run the available connection/pull operation and inspect the resulting dataset.

# Initial sync, historical imports and retention

Connector ingestion prioritizes the latest 90 days. It then backfills up to a
rolling three years of history that the provider actually makes available.
These are requests and limits, not a guarantee of three years of usable records.
questions: How much history is imported?
Why is only recent data available?
Is older data deleted?
title: Initial sync historical imports and retention

content:
Historical work is checkpointed and split into chunks, with background history
chunks capped at 30 days. Manual connector requests longer than 90 days are also
chunked. This bounds each ingestion task rather than making a single unbounded
historical request. The worker resumes its recorded progress; repeatedly
reconnecting or starting full overlapping imports is not a way to speed it up.

A recent dataset can be visible before backfill is complete. Check connection
progress and the dataset's actual dates before evaluating a three-year forecast
or concluding that older activity is missing from the provider.
questions: How much history is imported?
Why is only recent data available?
Is older data deleted?
title: Initial sync historical imports and retention

content:
Connector records older than the rolling three-calendar-year cutoff are removed
by the connector retention flow. Records with unusable dates cannot safely be
classified as old and may be retained. A historical summary cannot recreate
discarded transaction-level details.

Disconnecting a provider does not stop retention on its stored dataset.
The anomaly model's three-year lookback only limits what is used in a calculation.
Uploaded files expire as whole files based on upload date. Saved reports,
decisions and other workspace history expire based on when the records were
saved or created. The rolling limit does not close the workspace. Subscription
expiry and backup copies still have separate rules.

content:

work to finish before retrying. If it remains stuck, provide the connection and
workspace context through support, without tokens or raw private payloads.

# Choose relevant metrics

Dataset metric selection determines which measures can participate in analytical
workflows. Report metric selection is a further subset chosen for a particular
business question. A date column or dimension does not need to be a selected
numeric metric to serve its own purpose.
questions: Why are only some metrics preselected?
Does changing the objective replace manual choices?
Why did my selection not save?
title: Choose relevant metrics

content:
Business objectives shape automatic recommendations. When using system defaults,
changing the objective should resolve recommendations for the new objective,
rather than keeping unrelated automatic choices from the previous objective.
Deliberate manual selections, including an explicitly empty selection, must not
be silently overwritten by default-policy updates.

Accounting, commerce and payment defaults are restricted to reviewed
receipt/invoice measures emitted by that specific source/resource. This does not
mean every numeric field is a default, that every connector emits the same
receipt, or that internal costs and exchange rates must become metrics.

title: Choose relevant metrics

content:
Open dataset details, review the Business objective and recommendation/profile
information, choose the desired columns and save. Use Reset to system defaults
only when you intend to replace a manual selection. If a save is unconfirmed,
keep the draft and use the provided recovery control; do not assume a success
message or a failed request means the opposite without checking the saved state.

and saved policy. Empty values are not fabricated into a numeric field. A new
policy or missing normalized source field may require an explicit defaults reset
or successful resync, but those steps should follow diagnosis rather than be
promised as a universal fix.

Selection reduces the analytical surface. It is not a promise that every raw
unselected source field is absent from ingestion or memory at all stages.

# CRM and financial metric caveats

Use exact fields from the selected dataset. Provider documentation describes
possible fields; only inspection of an authorized dataset establishes which
fields and values that customer actually has.
questions: Is ProductQuantity a Salesforce field?
Why is TotalOpportunityQuantity missing?
Why can I not sum invoice totals for product rows?
Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
Reviewed Opportunity defaults include numeric Amount, ExpectedRevenue,
Probability and TotalOpportunityQuantity when present and eligible for the
selected objective/policy. Amount is estimated opportunity value, not necessarily
booked revenue. ExpectedRevenue is a weighted expected amount. Probability is
an estimated percentage, not an observed win rate and not a value to sum.

TotalOpportunityQuantity is the exact supported source name. Do not invent
ProductQuantity as an equivalent field. Quantity is opportunity-level context,
not proof that a per-product breakdown exists. A missing or entirely empty field
cannot be selected as a usable numeric metric; valid zeros and constants are not
the same as an absent field.
questions: Is ProductQuantity a Salesforce field?
Why is TotalOpportunityQuantity missing?
Why can I not sum invoice totals for product rows?
Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
Connector normalization can expand line items vertically rather than creating a
new horizontal set of columns for every item's position. This improves schema
stability but does not make an invoice-header total additive across every line.
Approved metric policies distinguish line amounts, document totals, distinct
counts and component-weighted ratios to avoid unsafe double counting.

A product filter that splits a transaction cannot arbitrarily allocate its
header total to the remaining lines. Choose a line-item measure or a
transaction-level dimension if the filter is rejected for splitting totals.

Why does Lightspeed show only quantity?
title: CRM and financial metric caveats

content:
Unresolved or mixed currencies can make a monetary metric ineligible. Do not
assume all money uses two decimal minor units, convert an already normalized
amount again, or infer profit/ROAS from unrelated totals. For Lightspeed, Zoho,
Sage or any other provider, inspect the exact series/resource and returned fields
before explaining a narrow default selection.

content:
# Dates, grouped periods and aggregation

Date selection, grouping and aggregation answer different questions. A Date
column identifies when source activity occurred. Start and End bound a manual
report. Analysis group by chooses the calendar buckets used for comparison.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
Daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly grouping collect observations into those
periods. One year of monthly records gives twelve monthly buckets. Choosing daily
grouping does not manufacture daily activity from monthly totals or fill missing
dates with trustworthy zeros.

Minimum historical observations counts usable matched grouped observations for
relationship testing. Reports and Relationships default to 30 observations and
daily grouping; valid saved settings are retained. A long form date range can still
have too few observations because the source is sparse, dates do not overlap,
filters remove rows, values do not vary or lagging removes matched pairs.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
Sum, average, minimum, maximum, count and curated policies have different
meanings. Use the policy appropriate to the measure. Ratios, distinct users,
opportunity probabilities, balances and document totals are not interchangeable
with additive sales amounts. Do not sum rates or repeated header totals just
because a chart can show a number.

Reports compare the selected window with the immediately preceding equal-length
window. Missing coverage may withhold a change; a zero comparison baseline may
make the percentage undefined. That is different from a measured zero change.
questions: What is a grouped period?
Does daily grouping create more observations?
Why are two pages showing different totals?
title: Dates grouped periods and aggregation

content:
Check that both pages use the same workspace, metric policy, date column, range,
dimension filter and grouping before comparing their values. Dashboards,
Forecasts, manual Reports and scheduled weekly Reports have separate time
controls. Weekly reporting follows completed weeks rather than retaining the
dates of the snapshot used as its template.

Analysis grouping is independent of weekly delivery. The weekly summary covers
the last completed Monday-Sunday week and checks daily coverage and unusual
changes. Its relationship analysis keeps the saved analysis grouping and lag
units. A weekly email can therefore include a monthly relationship analysis,
if enough matched monthly history is available. It does not relabel months as
days, change approved metric aggregation, or rewrite the saved snapshot.

# Filter metrics by category values

A dimension is contextual information such as channel, campaign, product,
customer, location or region. It filters the rows contributing to a metric; it
does not become a numerical outcome merely by being selected.

title: Filter metrics by category values

content:
1. On dashboards, open Filters beside the other controls. Business Analysis,
   Weekly Reports, Forecasts and Relationships provide their own date/dimension controls.
2. Review Date column and choose Dimension column.
3. Choose one or more Unique values from the dropdown. Search values narrows the
   list of choices; entering search text alone is not the selected-value filter.
4. Check the selected values and resulting data. Clear the dimension filter to
   return to all eligible rows. Closing a dashboard's Filters tab retains it.

The current report contract supports one dimension column per selected dataset,
with up to 50 selected values for that column. Report filters are dataset-local:
filtering one source's channel does not automatically find or filter equivalent
channels in another source. Relationships has independent filters for both sides.
Business impact setup instead offers one comparison dataset and one Unique value
for its dimension. Its Unique value control combines search and selection in one
dropdown. Type to filter choices, then select one; search alone does not change
the selected value. Selecting a different value replaces the current comparison
value. The decision supplies the outcome; any saved outcome segment is shown
read-only with a clear control. The comparison's Date column is beside Dimension
column; changing it recalculates the shared analysis period. The outcome Date
column is beside Outcome metric and starts with the saved selection. Business impact
analysis uses automatic history and grouping, displayed read-only rather than under
editable Analysis settings. Dimension filters do not invent missing matching records.
Decision assessment controls are in Business Analysis under Business impact, not Weekly Reports. Weekly monitoring
has its own dataset date and dimension selectors and automatic weekly dates and grouping.

mappings. Industry dashboard names describe a view, not proof that a connector's
schema contains every expected column. Confirm the mapping and units before
interpreting a tile as revenue, cost or conversion performance.

The dataset field combines search and selection. Typing narrows its list; choose
an option to change the dashboard's dataset. Leaving the field without choosing
keeps the existing selection. Clear dataset selection removes it explicitly.

Business Analysis is the on-demand analysis workspace. Multi-dataset report opens by
default; Single dataset report is available alongside it. Weekly Reports
has its own page and settings, automatic dates, whole-week and daily checks,
and earlier relationship history grouped weekly.

for the other workflow. Business Analysis has Build analysis and Analysis preview;
Weekly Reports has Report setup and Report preview. Business impact is a tool within

title: Build single and multi dataset reports

content:
Under Business Analysis > Compare metrics, choose one of two tabs:

- Multi-dataset report: select metrics from at least two datasets to review totals,
  trends and unusual changes. Enable correlation analysis is checked by default
  under Relationship analysis. Clear it to skip correlation and timing calculations
  and hide their controls and findings, while keeping summaries, charts and anomaly checks.
- Single dataset report: choose exactly one dataset, then its metrics, date column
  and optional dimension filter. It does not calculate cross-dataset relationships.

Both use the selected report dates and grouping, support dimension filters,
and require a preview before saving. Anomaly detection has Detect unusual changes
checked by default in both tabs; clear it to skip the detection calculations.
The seasonal-business choice is under a separate Business context section and
remains selectable while detection is off.
In both tabs, the editable Report name and optional Business question are at the
top of Build analysis, above the dataset and metric selection. Leaving the
question blank uses a default suited to the report: metric movements or
relationships. A custom question is kept and shown in the preview.
Missing metrics, dates, dimension values or invalid relationship settings are
explained beside Preview; those inputs must be resolved before running analysis.
The report name still has a unique default for one-off analysis and can be edited.
A saved report keeps its correlation and detection choices. Older relationship and
combined-metric reports both open under Multi-dataset report. This does not join
source rows or infer which metric caused another to change.
Copying a report with correlation disabled to Weekly Reports preserves its metric-only
setting; automatic weekly dates and weekly history still apply.

Joined datasets are excluded from both tabs: Multi-dataset report and
Single dataset report. Choose original datasets instead.

calculations and weekly setups, not to reading existing saved snapshots. If an
older setup contains joined sources, Remove joined datasets clears only those
sources and their dimension filters; the remaining selections are kept. Preview
again before saving a replacement. Dataset names are not used to decide whether
a source is joined.

provides the expected baseline, with reliability checked on records before the action;
the two results are not forced to have equal levels or identical seasonal behavior.
Earlier records must show that the comparison helps explain the outcome beyond
ordinary trends and calendar effects. Otherwise no impact amount is presented.

An extra yearly adjustment is considered only with about two years of pre-action
history. It must improve two earlier prediction checks before being used, and
the chosen baseline must then pass a separate held-back earlier-period check.
Records after the action are not used to choose the adjustment. A supported yearly
pattern cannot bypass missing-data, false-alarm, business-context or stability checks.
With shorter history, the report explicitly says that separate yearly differences
could not be checked reliably. Existing seasonal settings do not force or disable
this automatic impact-baseline choice; other report and forecast settings are unchanged.

The report answers whether the change appears to have helped, worked against the
goal, or remains unclear. It shows the estimated difference and a range, checks
earlier predictions and false alarms, and explains the next step in ordinary
business language. If the comparison fails the checks or other changes prevent
a fair comparison, no impact amount is presented. A range including zero means
the effect is unclear, not that the action definitely had no effect.
The range assumes the selected baseline is appropriate and does not cover every
uncertainty from choosing that baseline.

This is a model-based estimate under stated assumptions, not a randomized test
or automatic proof of cause and effect. New timed assessments compare actual
results with a baseline fitted before implementation; early and later results
can differ. They do not establish an exact causal delay, attribute an ad-spend
correlation alone, or rule out unknown concurrent events. Old standalone snapshots
can retain their original immediate, ongoing-level-change assumption. The main
answer is calculated directly, so an AI provider cannot invent
an impact amount or upgrade weak evidence. Details are available under the checks.
Supporting charts and unusual-change tables are kept in Supporting business
results, rather than crowding the main answer and decision links.

does not show Relationship findings. Its own comparison checks and estimated
impact are independent of the correlation settings. This applies to Business Impact
and Weekly Reports. Reopened older impact snapshots also omit their
old correlation findings from the preview; their stored calculations are not
rewritten or recalculated.

results. Timing, phase estimates and waiting status are included in weekly emails.

later deleted; new calculations cannot reuse a deleted or inaccessible source.

business change. Existing saved reports keep their original workflow.

title: Interpret relationships without assuming causation

content:
Business Analysis and Relationships include plain-language descriptions beside
the controls and results. Lead means the metric that changes first; lag is the
time between its change and the other metric's change. An observed lag is not a
promise of when a future business result will appear. A maximum lag or delay is
the furthest timing gap to test, measured in the selected grouping's days, weeks,
months or quarters, not a promised response time.

The correlation coefficient describes how closely the two metrics move together.
Near +1 means they tend to rise and fall together; near -1 means they tend to
move in opposite directions. Near zero means no clear pattern of the kind tested.
It is not a percentage change, revenue per dollar, or proof that one metric
caused the other to change. Existing reliability and missing-history warnings
still apply even when a coefficient is shown.

Anomaly detection is a different check: unusually high or low results within a
metric compared with its earlier history. A flag is a reason to check, not proof
of a problem. Expected busy and quiet seasons are considered only when seasonal
adjustment is enabled and supported by enough history. Business Analysis runs
these checks when enabled; Relationships explains the distinction but does not
run anomaly detection.

content:
Business Analysis and Weekly Reports display the Correlation coefficient and Lag

detailed explanation. Relationships shows these values in the opened saved
result too. Positive lags include their time unit and metric order. A valid
same-period result shows 0 (same period); a missing coefficient is not displayed
as zero, and insufficient evidence does not imply zero lag.

Changing direction on an existing preview in Business Analysis or Relationships
recalculates it automatically. A spinner and Processing message appear beside
the dropdown, which is disabled until the calculation finishes. The previous
evidence remains visible; a failed update keeps the old result and direction so
you can retry. Updating a preview does not silently save a report or relationship.
On Relationships, a direction choice before the first preview only configures
the comparison; Preview relationship starts the calculation.

Lag units follow the relationship analysis grouping, not the chart's detail:
weekly relationship history produces a lag in weeks even when the report week
is also shown day by day. A tentative lag is still an observed result, not a
dependable response time; check the accompanying timing warning.

Consider the sign and magnitude of the coefficient, matched observation count,
timing, significance information, coverage and warnings together. A coefficient
near zero is not proof that the systems are unrelated in every possible way.
A strong coefficient can reflect a shared trend, seasonality, duplicates or
mathematically related measures rather than an independent business influence.

Report relationships use historical context of at least 90 calendar days ending
at the report's end, or a longer requested window, with the matched-observation
threshold applied after grouping and filtering. Weekly relationships use their
own rolling history. The value being compared for last week's KPI is not simply
correlated across seven daily points without a historical check.

Significance is adjusted across tested pairs and lags where the supported
statistical backend and inputs permit it. An unavailable significance value must
not be described as a passing test. Time-series autocorrelation and selecting
the best observed lag still limit interpretation.

each selected spending metric with revenue across matched dates. Choose which
metric is expected to come first for each pair if you want to test delayed
movement. Review the coefficient, observed delay, shared history and warnings.
This shows historical association, not revenue earned for each dollar spent.

For better value from money already spent, use Return on spend with consistently
assigned channel revenue and spending. Do not rank channels by correlation and
call the result return on investment. A channel can move closely with revenue
but cost much more. For a future spending mix, use Budget Planner; for a
recorded action's estimated effect, use Business impact with a fair unaffected
comparison and the required earlier evidence. Chat cannot choose your winner
without running the relevant workspace analysis.

higher values of the other at the tested timing. A negative coefficient means
they tended to move in opposite directions. Values run from -1 to 1; a value
near zero means little association of the kind tested, not proof of no business
connection. Not available is missing evidence, not a coefficient of zero.

Positive does not automatically mean good: costs and complaints can rise together.
Negative can be desirable, such as shorter waits accompanying higher satisfaction.
The coefficient is not a percentage revenue increase or a return per dollar.
Common seasons, overall growth or other changes can explain movement together.
Use the finding to decide what to investigate or test, not as proof of causation.

# Timing, direction and minimum observations

Lag is the number of grouped calendar periods by which one series is shifted
relative to another. A lag of 2 means two days with daily grouping, two weeks
with weekly grouping, two months with monthly grouping, or two quarters with
quarterly grouping. It is not automatically a two-day conversion delay.
questions: Does maximum lag test every day up to 365?
How do I set direction for a middle metric?
Why is a one-year report insufficient?
title: Timing direction and minimum observations

content:
Enable correlation analysis is checked by default in Multi-dataset report.
When enabled, Delay to check and Maximum delay appear above Metric pairs.
Relationship direction defaults to Automatic (recommended): marketing leads,
sales follows, and other sources need stable historical predictive timing.
If no dependable leader is found, the preview says Not established and shows
the same-period relationship. Choose either named metric to override the suggestion.
A metric can follow
one metric and lead another; there is no need to assign one global direction to
the middle source.

Remove relationship pairs you do not want to analyze. Removed pairs are excluded
from relationship tests and cross-dataset movement contrasts, including in weekly
reports using that template. Restore a pair from Removed pairs to reuse its
previous direction. Removing a pair does not deselect its metrics: KPI and
anomaly analysis still assess each selected metric. Removing all pairs runs no
relationship tests. Removing a metric also clears exclusions involving it, so
reselecting that metric creates its pairs again.

The interface no longer offers Test both directions or Same-period comparison only. Directional timing includes
lag zero and eligible positive lags up to the selected maximum of 12 periods.
The maximum is not a search of every day from 1 to 365. A maximum lag of
zero also restricts every retained pair to its same-period test.

title: Timing direction and minimum observations

content:
Reports and Relationships share a default minimum of 30 matched observations
and daily grouping, not 30 dates in the form. Explicit saved grouping and
thresholds are retained, including the previously saved 24-observation setting.
The editable minimum remains 24; 30 is the new default, not a new lower bound. Twelve
monthly source points fail that threshold. Filtering, non-overlapping dates,
missing buckets and shifting for lag can reduce the usable pair further.
The minimum must still be met after lagging. Positive-lag searches therefore
need more source history than a same-period comparison at the same threshold.
Constant or otherwise unsuitable series can prevent meaningful correlation even
when the nominal point count is large enough.

New report lag tests shift calendar buckets before dropping missing pairs. They
do not treat two neighboring surviving observations as adjacent calendar days
when dates between them were missing. Group more finely only if the source has
real observations at that finer frequency; do not manufacture history to pass a
threshold.

The best observed lag is a historical association under the selected tests.
Business timing knowledge should guide the hypothesis, and later independent
observations or an experiment should test it.

# Saved relationships versus report relationships

Relationships is a separate page for a saved monitor comparing two metrics from
different datasets. Multi dataset report is the broader review workflow with
multiple metrics, period movements, anomalies and cross-source findings.

title: Saved relationships versus report relationships

content:
Choose the left and right datasets and their metrics. Review both Date columns
and apply each side's Dimension column and Unique values independently when
needed. Set the period and aggregation to fit the business question, then check
the actual overlapping source dates.

Preview relationship first, review the evidence, then choose Save relationship
below the result. Changing a dataset, metric, date column, dimension filter or
analysis setting clears the old preview; preview again before saving. An opened
saved relationship does not need to be saved again unless its setup changes.
Missing selections appear beside the preview action. Refresh reloads available
datasets and saved relationships without resetting valid selections. If columns
fail to load, use Retry dataset columns.

New analyses on both pages default to Spearman, daily grouping, Sum aggregation
where applicable, 30 minimum historical observations, a maximum lag of 12 grouped
periods, and automatic direction. Correlation method, Minimum historical
observations and Maximum lag are visible in Relationship analysis rather than
hidden in advanced options. Valid deliberately saved settings are retained.

Leave Relationship direction at Automatic (recommended) to suggest the leader.
Marketing sources lead and sales sources follow. When those categories do not
choose an order, Decisionate checks predictive timing in earlier and later history,
accounting for trend and recurring calendar patterns where enough history exists.
If the direction is not dependable, the result says Not established and shows a
same-period comparison, not an invented leader. The preview explains the suggestion.
Choose either named metric to override it and preview again before saving. A
chosen direction evaluates zero through Maximum lag. Dataset labels and each
source's dimension filter retain their original identities when the second
metric leads. The 12-period maximum is the same for daily, weekly, monthly and
quarterly grouping; it is not an automatic conversion into days.

There is no new fixed-lag editor. Existing saved fixed-lag monitors retain their
original timing, shown as Saved fixed lag, until the user explicitly chooses a
new direction. Saved grouping and observation thresholds, including weekly
grouping and a 24-observation threshold, are not overwritten by the new defaults.

The observation minimum is enforced after filtering, grouping and lagging.
Insufficient observations produce insufficient data, not a usable correlation.
Observation and lag limits persist with each monitor and are reused for its
scheduled evaluation. Existing monitors without a saved history threshold use
24 for backward compatibility; newly created analyses default to 30. Read the
matched periods, timing, strength and credibility before
saving. Shared defaults do not make the two workflows identical: the saved
monitor retains its fixed/automatic timing and stability scoring, while Reports
supports multiple pairs and its report-specific calendar alignment and testing
limits. Neither workflow proves causation.

content:
# Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

Anomaly detection checks whether a metric is unusually high or low compared with
its expected range based on earlier history. It is not simply the percentage
change from the previous period and does not establish why a change happened.

Multi-dataset report and Single dataset report each have
an Anomaly detection section. Detect unusual changes is checked by default for
new reports and when editing older reports without an explicit choice. Clear it
to skip the detection calculations while retaining totals, trends, earlier-period
comparisons and any requested relationship analysis. Preview again after changing
it, then save; saved reports and copies to Weekly Reports retain the choice.

Business has seasonal activity is a separate, opt-in setting under Business
context, above the Anomaly detection section. It remains selectable when
detection is off, and its preference is retained. It affects anomaly checks
when they run; it does not adjust correlations. An off report says Anomaly detection is off for this report;
it does not claim No unusual changes detected or hide the choice as missing data.

When enabled, report anomaly detection assesses each selected metric separately. It runs
independently of whether relationship analysis finds an eligible or significant
pair. No unusual change detected is a valid outcome; it is not proof that a
worker failed.

When detection is enabled, weekly reports assess the last completed Monday-Sunday in two ways: the whole
week against earlier complete weeks, and individual days against their daily
baseline. Each selected metric has separate results for both. A normal weekly
value can hide unusual daily ups and downs; a run of small daily changes can
produce an unusual week. Whole-week results include an expected range even
when the week is not unusual. Missing dates prevent a complete-week assessment;
they are not replaced with invented zero values.
questions: Is anomaly detection MAD or standard deviation?
Does the seasonal checkbox force a seasonal model?
Does no unusual change mean the engine failed?
title: Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

content:
The detector uses preceding history inside a rolling three-calendar-year cap.
An assessed block is held out of its own training data. It fits a robust trend
and, when Business has seasonal activity is enabled, considers supported calendar
patterns. Seasonal terms must improve past-only validation; the checkbox does
not force a seasonal model onto every metric.

Annual patterns need at least two preceding annual cycles plus validation data
and adequate coverage. Three years selected in a form does not guarantee that
three years of suitable observations exist. Missing source activity is not
automatically treated as measured zero, and holidays and promotions are not
automatically known events.
questions: Is anomaly detection MAD or standard deviation?
Does the seasonal checkbox force a seasonal model?
Does no unusual change mean the engine failed?
title: Unusual changes and seasonal businesses

content:
The primary variability measure is scaled median absolute deviation of held-out
baseline residuals. Standard deviation of residuals is a fallback when MAD is
too small. If both are effectively constant, the method records a constant
residual rather than pretending that a reliable non-zero spread exists.
This is not simply calculating the standard deviation of all raw values.

content:
Review actual value, expected value, expected range, deviation, direction and
the history/model warnings. The displayed range is an exploratory anomaly
threshold, not a guaranteed confidence interval or proof of a business cause.
Limited history or unassessed observations must not be reported as no anomalies.

Check imports, filters, date choices and structural changes first. If the
change warrants action, create a human-reviewed decision and later record its
outcome. The lookback cap excludes old data from fitting; connector retention
is the separate process that can delete old source records.

content:
Select the sales metric in Business Analysis for a chosen period, or Weekly
Reports for the last completed week. Unusual-change detection compares each
selected metric with its expected behavior, even if no relationship pair is
tested. Check actual value, expected range and history warnings. A change may
be unusual without its cause being known.

First check incomplete imports, date and dimension filters, closures, promotions
and other known changes. Seasonal activity can help account for supported
recurring patterns, but it does not automatically know a holiday or campaign.
Relationship findings can suggest another metric to investigate; they do not
prove why sales changed. No unusual change detected differs from Not assessed:
the latter means evidence was insufficient, not that sales were normal.

content:

also checks the individual days. A sharp rise and fall can cancel out over the
week. Conversely, several small daily increases can add up to an unusual week.
Both assessments are useful and neither should be substituted for the other.

Missing dates prevent a complete-week assessment; they are not assumed to be
days with zero business. Read the history and seasonal warnings before acting.
The expected range describes usual behavior under the available evidence, not
a sales target or a promise. An unusual change does not by itself send an
immediate alert; weekly email delivery is controlled separately.

# Forecast a selected metric

Forecasts estimates future values using observed source history. It is separate
from Business Analysis, which reviews evidence and relationships over historical periods.
A projection is not a commitment that the business will achieve that outcome.

title: Forecast a selected metric

content:
1. Open Forecasts and choose or search for the intended dataset, then select its metric.
2. Review Date column beside Dimension column. Select Unique values if the
   forecast should cover a segment rather than all eligible rows.
3. Choose the history range, grouping and aggregation appropriate to the source.
4. Enable Business has seasonal activity when recurring calendar patterns matter.
5. Review the forecast, historical series, model basis, validation and warnings.

The forecast uses the selected date field and dimension filter. Dashboard period
defaults do not silently define a forecast's history. A filter can leave too
little history even when the unfiltered dataset looks large.

Seasonal candidates use a bounded history of up to three years and past-only
validation. Annual patterns need enough preceding cycles and coverage. Trend-only
or non-seasonal fallback can be appropriate when seasonal support is not
established. Read the stated basis rather than assuming the checkbox guarantees
a seasonal model or that a fallback has the same capabilities.

content:
If Forecast unavailable says the date column needs a year, its values include
month names or month/day labels without a year. Forecasts cannot infer the real
year from labels such as Jan or 01/15. Choose another date column with years or
update the dataset with the actual dates, for example 2025-01. Retrying unchanged
data will not resolve this validation issue. No year is guessed for you.

Validation errors describe performance on the available held-out history, not a
guaranteed future error bound. Gaps, changing business conditions, source delays
and exceptional events can undermine a forecast. Do not infer promotions or
holidays that were not provided as facts.

An API that does not support a requested seasonal, date or dimension policy
should not silently satisfy it with a different calculation. Preserve the
selection, retry after a confirmed service recovery and escalate persistent
unavailability. Forecasts were not moved into the Reports analysis-worker queue;
healthy report-worker status alone does not verify forecasting.

failure. Retry dataset load reloads the dataset list when no dataset is selected.

then read the projected dates, trend, model basis and warnings. Filtering can

predict the effect of a proposed price, staffing or advertising change. Budget
Planner handles supported future spending scenarios; Cash flow planning uses
expected receipts and payment dates. A sales projection alone is neither a
complete cash plan nor an inventory purchase recommendation. Ask Decisionate
can explain the setup but does not read your sales or produce an account-specific
forecast in chat.

enough: repeated cycles and adequate observations must support the pattern.

or exceptional holiday demand. Check coverage, validation and the stated model
basis, then use business judgment for events outside that evidence. Historical

content:
# Configure Weekly Reports

Weekly reports are cross-dataset reviews, not a repeated single-metric screenshot.
Open Weekly Reports in the sidebar. It requires usable metrics from at least
two datasets for delivery. Business Analysis is a separate page and does not
control the weekly report's dates or time grouping.
The pages do not share a workflow tab bar. Weekly Reports uses Report
setup and Report preview; Business Analysis uses Build analysis and Analysis preview.
questions: Do saved report dates fix the weekly dates?
Does choosing a template enable sending?
Does scheduler success mean delivered?
title: Configure a meaningful weekly report

content:
Open Analysis -> Weekly Reports. Select metrics, date columns, dimension filters,
seasonal setting and relationship pairs. Report details contains the editable
name and optional business question. If the question is blank, the report asks
what changed last week and what needs attention next. Choose Preview report.
Previewing calculates the draft without changing the saved weekly setup or sending email.
After a successful preview, choose Save changes. Each workspace has one current
weekly report. Saving replaces that report and its setup for future weeks,
even if you change its name; it does not create another active report.
The default name is Weekly Business Report, not a random identifier. You can
use a custom name; it stays the same when the report is updated. Existing
generated names are replaced in the current setup and future reports, while
historical reports and decision evidence keep their original names.
There is no separate Save snapshot or Save weekly settings action on this page.
Changing the setup requires another preview before saving. A failed preview or
save leaves the previously saved setup unchanged. If the reporting week, source
data or saved setup changes before saving, generate a fresh preview.
Weekly history contains sent reports and previously saved legacy reports, not
alternative active setups. Opening history does not replace the current setup.
Reports already sent and evidence attached to decisions stay unchanged when
the current report is replaced. Sent-report history is recorded automatically
for new deliveries; old delivery logs cannot reconstruct missing report contents.
Removed pairs remain excluded
from weekly relationship analysis, while their selected metrics still receive
KPI and anomaly analysis. Saving a weekly report enables automatic email to the
workspace owner every Monday when the report has sufficient data. No recipient
configuration is needed. Explicitly paused schedules remain paused when the
report is edited; saving never sends an immediate email or changes additional addresses.

In the preview, This week at a glance is followed by What deserves attention,
before the detailed charts. Each priority finding includes its supported next
step and result to track. Create decision opens the central form with that
finding's evidence; it does not execute an action or assume improvement.
View existing decision opens an already-linked decision instead of duplicating it.
Supporting evidence and Expected result and limitations remain available with
the finding. An incomplete report states its coverage problem at the top and
does not offer new decision creation or email delivery. Detailed metric charts,
relationship evidence, decision progress and source quality remain available.

A saved business analysis offers Copy selection to Weekly Reports. This is an
editable copy, not a live link. Non-weekly timing choices reset to same-period
comparison, with a default maximum of 12 weeks; a three-day lag is not converted
to three weeks. Preview and save the independent weekly setup before use.

In Weekly Reports, use Scheduled email to add optional additional addresses, change the delivery day,
timezone, email readiness and delivery history. Save email settings updates only
delivery preferences, not report selections. The status reflects the saved
schedule; unsaved changes are labeled separately. The workspace owner is always
included, including the client owner in a managed client workspace. An owner
listed among additional addresses receives only one copy. Automatic delivery can
be paused. Opening this page does not run another analysis.
A test email is a delivery check without report results or data requirements,
sent to the workspace owner and any saved additional addresses, even while delivery is paused.
Save recipient changes before testing. Successful saves clear their notice after
five seconds; failures remain visible. Earlier metric-email selections and targets
are preserved; new report content is configured and previewed in Weekly Reports.
A successful scheduler invocation means a job was queued, not that an email was
delivered. Check terminal analysis status and delivery history separately.

Email workspace owner (previously Send report now) emails the current weekly report only to the workspace owner,
including the client owner in a managed client workspace. First preview and save
the current weekly report. Sending does not save unsaved changes. This one-time
send can run while scheduled delivery is paused;
it does not change recipients, enable delivery or replace a scheduled send.
Only authorized workspace managers can use it. If the owner's account has no
usable email address, sending is blocked rather than using another recipient.

Sending requires usable data from at least two selected datasets in the last
completed week. If the preview has insufficient coverage, Send report now is
disabled and shows the exact dates needed. Sync or upload data for that week,
then preview again. Historical demo files belong in Business Analysis; weekly
reports do not shift to the most recent dates in an old file. Saved weekly
settings load only their selected datasets, not unrelated workspace sources.

After a confirmed failure before delivery starts, a deliberate retry starts a
fresh attempt. If delivery might have started, check delivery history before
trying again. Uncertain status reads keep the same request to avoid duplicates.
When the server confirms report preparation stopped before delivery, the page
explicitly says no email was sent. Older attempts without that confirmation
remain conservative; they are not silently resent.

KPI targets are benchmark context for the digest and interpretation. Setting a
target does not by itself create a separate immediate threshold-triggered alert.
Use the current delivery settings rather than assuming every metric anomaly
causes an instant email.

Each run reviews the latest completed Monday-Sunday week in the platform
reporting timezone, compared with the preceding week. The manual report's Start
and End are not a permanent weekly window. Historical context rolls with the
current run date and is capped at three years where used for weekly analysis.

The last completed week's charts and unusual-change checks use daily detail:
one point for each Monday-Sunday date. KPI totals still cover the full week and
are compared with the preceding full week. A separate Whole-week assessment
checks each selected metric's full-week value against its expected weekly range,
using earlier complete weeks and seasonal adjustment when supported. Daily
changes and whole-week results can differ: opposing daily changes may cancel
out, or small daily changes may add up to an unusual week. Incomplete weeks are
excluded rather than treating missing dates as zero. If there is not enough
usable weekly history, the whole-week assessment is labeled unassessed.
Both views are included in the preview and email, and supplied as bounded facts
for interpretation. Earlier relationship history is
grouped into complete weekly periods, ending on the Sunday before the report
week; daily points are not mixed into the weekly relationship series.
There is no manual Start/End or Group by selector on the weekly page. Relationship
defaults are Spearman, 30 minimum matched weeks, same-period comparison, and a
maximum directional lag of 12 weeks. The minimum can be changed independently
within allowed bounds. Lag zero compares the same week. The selected metric's
approved aggregation policy is preserved: weekly grouping does not turn every
metric into a sum. Per-metric anomaly results include seasonal support and history warnings.

Changing Business Analysis dates, daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly grouping, or timing
settings does not change the saved weekly settings. Changing weekly settings does
not alter Business Analysis or either workflow's saved snapshots.

assessments in Business Analysis under Business impact, or open Assess business impact from Decision Details.
Weekly Reports focuses on selected metrics, unusual changes and relationships.
Old weekly decision links open Business impact within Business Analysis. Older explicit copy links copy
only metrics and dimension filters, not the assessment; the Business impact tool
does not offer a Copy selection to Weekly Reports action.

or deleted. Their setup is read-only, with an Open Business impact link.

same selected metrics. The existing weekly configuration is replaced only after
preview and Save changes; saved decision assessments and report history remain.
Simply opening the page, following the link or previewing does not change the saved
weekly configuration. Changes in Business Impact do not silently update that configuration.

An existing assessment's weekly preview includes a short Decision update with
the assessment period and a link to the decision, when available. Its evidence
remains available under Assessment evidence. The weekly email retains its answer,
estimated range when available, and next steps. It keeps the original change date,
result and unaffected comparison. Its study uses weekly grouping, starting at the rolling
three-year cutoff and ending with the latest completed week. It needs at least
52 complete weeks before the change and 8 after, plus the other comparison checks.
This is separate from the email's seven-day KPI totals; it does not attempt to
estimate a business impact from seven days alone.
An impact report keeps its own comparison checks and anomaly detection, but
does not also run an exploratory correlation or include Relationship findings
in its preview or email. A monitoring configuration checks selected relationships.
Previewing or emailing a weekly report does not create a decision or overwrite
its outcome. Explicitly saving a linked assessment attaches it to the selected
decision. Existing standalone weekly studies can continue under their original
saved configuration; new assessments require selecting a decision on Business Impact.

As old history leaves the three-year window, the study can lose enough earlier
data to support an estimate. The email then explains the missing evidence rather
than repeating an old number. The original saved snapshot remains unchanged.

# Create decisions and track outcomes

A decision records a concrete action, its reasoning, expected result and later
outcome. Reading a report, finding a correlation or generating an AI recommendation
does not automatically create an accountable decision.

content:
You can create a decision without leaving Business Analysis. On a completed
Compare metrics report, choose Create decision. With two usable metrics, track
two metric targets or choose to review the result yourself. With one usable
metric, record your action, expected result and review date. The report keeps
the link to the decision. On Return on spend, Profitability, Customer retention,
Sales conversion and Cash flow planning, use Create decision on the results.
The comparison is saved as evidence automatically when you submit.

Business impact starts with an existing decision. Save an assessment to keep it
with that decision. If the assessment produces an estimate and you want to take
a different action, create a follow-up decision; this does not replace the first.
Weekly Reports, saved budget plans and the Decisions page also have creation
entries. Use the action you actually plan to take, not just the report name.

The form shows the next missing requirement beside Create decision. A
report-linked decision needs a ready report, an outcome metric, a meaningful
name, action, expected result, reasoning and a review date. Changing these fields
does not automatically submit the decision. If a request fails, the entered
details remain available for retry; an existing recommendation-linked decision
should be opened rather than created again.

A report-linked decision should retain the selected evidence metrics, report
identity and relevant limitations, not expand to every metric in its datasets.
An outcome metric is a measurement choice within the supported evidence scope,
not a reason to include unrelated source columns.

content:
In Create decision, use **Measure an action and a result**. For example, choose
ad spend as the action, Increase, Percentage, 10. Choose orders as the result,
Increase, Amount, 20. Enter the day the change starts and the date to review it.
Choose **Preview targets** to see the actual baseline, target and dates for
each metric. A baseline of 100 orders gives a target of 120 orders in this
example. A percentage target needs a nonzero baseline; use an amount instead
when starting from zero. If a comparable decision has already been measured in
this workspace, the preview links to its result before you commit to a new one.

You can choose metrics directly or use a saved report. Report-linked plans
keep its date columns, calculations, filters and timezone. If its earlier
relationship analysis supports a delay between this action and result, the
result window starts after that delay. Review compares each window with the
same number of days immediately before the change. The review date itself is
not counted: the last measurement day is the day before review.

Open decisions are checked on or after the review date, both in the background
and when opened. Missing days are not counted as zero. Each target is shown
separately: spending can reach its target even if orders do not. Complete
results appear in Action Needed and in matching weekly reports with a decision
link. The owner can close the decision to keep the last assessment. Meeting a
target does not prove that the action caused the change. Choose **Review
manually** for qualitative decisions or where daily records aren't available.

content:

and choose Business impact. The assessment setup reuses
the recorded action and outcome metric, and asks for the actual action start
date, an unaffected comparison from another dataset and the business context.

Choose Save assessment to decision after reviewing the calculation. It attaches
one assessment to the existing decision and preserves its report snapshot.

create a second decision. Assessment history stays on Business impact review.

and does not automatically complete or mark the decision successful.

Compare before and after is the older simple metric comparison, not the
cross-dataset impact model. Its percentage change is not a causal impact estimate.
Keep that distinction when recording what actually happened.

For a manual decision, record the actual outcome, its status and a specific lesson at review time.
Document confounding factors instead of claiming a change was caused by the
decision solely because it followed it. Historical learning uses recorded
workspace evidence; it is not automatic retraining of the model.

authorized lifecycle controls and read confirmations. Deleting a report does not
delete the decisions linked to that report.

using that data. Permanently deleting a decision removes its attached assessment

assessments whose source datasets they are authorized to access.

# AI interpretation and rules fallback

The statistical engines compute metric comparisons, anomaly evidence and
relationship tests. AI interpretation explains the supplied evidence
and suggests risks or follow-up actions. The AI does not create missing
observations, change statistical results or prove a causal business explanation.

content:
Generate a fresh report preview to request interpretation automatically. There
is no Include AI interpretation checkbox in the report builder. This also applies
when editing an older report whose definition disabled interpretation. A
previously saved snapshot keeps its original narrative; opening it or adding
provider credentials does not rerun AI or rewrite its history.

Provider configuration, a supported model/endpoint, workspace AI credits and
service availability affect whether an external AI response can be obtained.
The current implementation supports an OpenAI provider adapter; this static
article does not certify a currently available model or a particular account's
provider access.

content:
A source of rules means deterministic fallback, not an external AI response.
Missing configuration, an unsupported provider, exhausted credits or a failed
provider request triggers fallback for report previews without blocking the
computed metric, anomaly and relationship results. A
successful report or Configured status alone does not prove external AI ran.

Provider and model names can be displayed without an API key. A key is required
to call the provider, not to render those names. Customer users should not add
platform credentials or paste a secret into chat; configuration is an operator
responsibility.
